correctness.rationale: For Pareto scale a>0, shape alpha>2, mu=alpha a/(alpha-1), sigma=a sqrt(alpha)/((alpha-1)sqrt(alpha-2)), so mu-sigma<a since sqrt(alpha/(alpha-2))>1. Therefore the standardized one-sigma central mass equals 1-A_alpha^-alpha, where A_alpha=alpha/(alpha-1)*(1+1/sqrt(alpha(alpha-2))). For x>0 log(1+x)>x/(1+x); applied to 1/(alpha-1) and 1/sqrt(alpha(alpha-2)), each contributes >1/alpha to log A, giving alpha log A>2. As alpha->infinity, log A=2/alpha+1/alpha^2+7/(6alpha^3)+..., hence central mass=1-e^-2+e^-2/alpha+O(alpha^-2). Strict inequality and convergence establish sharp unattained infimum for all scales/shapes, not a generic Chebyshev bound. Independently evaluated 7 shapes including alpha=10000; finite checks corroborate.
